newsitem.title: UK: BG has no regrets over going to MMC - Varne.
newsitem.headline: BG has no regrets over going to MMC - Varne.

text.p: David Varney, Chief Executive of BG plc, said on Wednesday he had no regrets over pipeline operator Transco's decision to appeal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) over the Transco pricing regime proposed by industry regulator Ofgas.
"This is a tough report," Varney told a news conference. "There are bits in it we think are good, there are other bits frankly I'm disappointed with."
But he added that on balance it allowed both sides, Transco and industry regulator Ofgas, to go forward "with honour."

He repeated several times that even with the benefit of hindsight, BG would still have taken the decision to appeal Ofgas' pricing proposals to the MMC rather than accepting them in the form Ofgas proposed last autumn.
The board had been unanimous in its decision to go to the MMC, he said. BG's costs in presenting its case to the MMC were around 10 million stg, which the company said was money well spent.
Clare Spottiswoode, Director General of Gas Supply, told a news conference earlier that Ofgas' costs had been around one million stg.

Financial director Philip Hampton highlighted the fact that under the MMC recommendations, Transco will gain 220 million stg in revenues over five years more than it would have done under Ofgas' proposals last year.
"In narrow financial terms we believe it (the MMC referral) has paid us back many times over," he added.

The MMC has now established a Regulatory Asset Base for Transco of 11.6 billion stg, which with an allowed return of seven percent suggests Transco can earn 812 million per year. "If we can outperform the formula we will do better," said Varney.
He was clearly concerned that the government's proposed windfall tax on utilities could have an adverse impact.
"I just hope the Treasury will read this document from cover to cover. It's a tough document and there's no provision in it for the windfall tax," he said.
He declined to speculate on possible job cuts in Transco resulting from the MMC's report.

When Ofgas first published its proposals, BG said that they would lead to a loss of revenue equivalent to 10,000 job losses. Since then, 3,500 jobs went through voluntary redundancies last year and a further 1,000 in the first quarter of this year.
Varney would not say if more losses were inevitable, insisting that BG needed time to digest the full impact of the report.
Around 16,000 people now work at Transco, he said. The GMB union has already said it saw job losses as a "logical possibility" following the publication of the report.
Varney said no decision would be taken on whether or not BG plc would be able to pay a dividend to shareholders until publication of the half yearly results in September.
He would not join a debate on whether either Ofgas or BG had won following the MMC's report, saying "you can never build a sensible relationship on the basis of triumphalism on one side or another."
